method: Direct header, implementation and class-test audit; no C++ build or execution. The class test's own expectations are platform-derived, so the same derivations are reproduced rather than pinned to one host.
evidence_tier: tier 3 (source review, transcribed class-test expectations) and tier 4 (independently derived name tables, pointer-width derivation and build-configuration constants)

source_surface.counting_rule: Public function declarations in the header, constructors and destructors counted separately: Internal::getOSVersionString_ (1), OpenMSOSInfo::getOSAsString / getArchAsString / getOSVersionAsString / getBinaryArchitecture / getActiveSIMDExtensions / getOSInfo (6), OpenMSBuildInfo::isOpenMPEnabled / getBuildType / getOpenMPMaxNumThreads / setOpenMPNumThreads (4). OpenMSOSInfo declares one explicit default constructor; there is no user-declared destructor.

source_anchors.operation: OpenMS_OS and OpenMS_Architecture each end in a SIZE_OF_* sentinel that exists only to size the parallel inline name array indexed by the enum value
getOSVersionString_ uses RtlGetVersion from ntdll.dll on Windows, sysctlbyname("kern.osproductversion") on macOS and VERSION_ID from /etc/os-release on other Unix, returning "unknown" on any failure
the Unix branch prefix-matches "VERSION_ID=" and strips one surrounding pair of double quotes only when the value is at least two characters long
getBinaryArchitecture switches on sizeof(size_t) and can return "unknown", unlike getOSInfo

getOSInfo sets the OS from WIN32 / (__MACH__ && __APPLE__) / __unix__ in that order, so every non-macOS Unix reports Linux, and derives the architecture from sizeof(void*) with 4 meaning 32-bit and everything else 64-bit
isOpenMPEnabled, getOpenMPMaxNumThreads and setOpenMPNumThreads compile to false, 1 and a no-op when _OPENMP is not defined
getBuildType returns the configure-time OPENMS_BUILD_TYPE macro from build_config.h
getActiveSIMDExtensions pushes neon, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2 and FMA in that order from the SIMDe arch probes and joins them with ", "

class_test_review.literal_extraction: The three "unknown" defaults and the seven name-table labels are transcribed. The binary-architecture and OS-probe sections are derived exactly as the source test derives them, from sizeof(size_t) and from the accepted set {Windows, MacOS, Linux}; the SIMD section asserts only the determinism the source test asserts, plus that every emitted label is one of the nine the source can emit.

native_boundaries: The SIZE_OF_* enum sentinels and both inline name arrays have no counterpart: OperatingSystem::as_str and Architecture::as_str replace the array and the index into it
OsInfo exposes public fields where the source keeps private members behind get*AsString accessors; the labels remain available through the enums

os_version_string reads /etc/os-release under cfg(target_os = "linux") and reports "unknown" everywhere else, because RtlGetVersion and sysctlbyname need a platform binding this crate does not take; that cfg is narrower than the source's __unix__ branch, so a non-Linux Unix that publishes /etc/os-release reports "unknown" here while the source would read it - the OS name is unaffected, since the port maps every non-macOS Unix to Linux as the source does; /etc/os-release reads are capped at 64 KiB

active_simd_extensions reads Rust target features instead of the SIMDe build macros, keeping the source's order and labels; the port has no hand-written SIMD, so the value reports only what the compiler was allowed to emit
openmp_enabled is always false and openmp_max_num_threads always 1, matching the source's non-OpenMP build exactly
setOpenMPNumThreads is not ported: it is a no-op in a non-OpenMP build and there is no thread pool here to size
build_type is derived from debug_assertions, since Cargo bakes no profile name into a library; it separates the stock dev and release profiles but follows the setting rather than the profile's name
OsInfo::detect reproduces the source's pointer-width rule verbatim, including that anything other than four bytes is reported as 64-bit
openmp_gap: This header is the port's only place where OpenMP is visible at all, and it is visible as its absence: no OpenMP runtime is linked, so the two reported values are the source's own non-OpenMP answers and the setter is dropped. The answers depend on _OPENMP alone, which is what the source's own predicate tests, so they do not change if the crate threads work by other means.
